 SpaceX Stock Adds $54 Billion Amid Viral AI in Space Discussions
 Lockridge Okoth Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:02 PM EST 2 min read SPCX -4.56% 
 Trade SPCX on Coinbase Trading disclosure Trading disclosure 
 The above button links to Coinbase. Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading. Coinbase pays us for certain activity generated through this link. Prices displayed are informational. 
 Learn more SpaceX added roughly $54 billion in market value on Tuesday afternoon as investors backed Elon Musk's ambitious plan to move artificial intelligence data centers into space. 
 Shares rose nearly 3%, following fresh comments from chief financial officer Bret Johnsen. He believes SpaceX could become one of the world's largest AI infrastructure providers as early as 2027. 
 SpaceX Stock Intraday Chart — November 17. Source: Yahoo Finance Can SpaceX Make AI Data Centers Work in Space? 
 Speaking at the TomorrowX summit in Austin, Johnsen outlined plans to launch solar-powered computing satellites using Starship, SpaceX's reusable rocket. 
 Initial satellites could fly in 2027, with deployments expanding in 2028 and meaningful computing capacity arriving in 2029. 
 The financial argument is straightforward. Data centers on Earth face rising electricity bills, cooling costs and land constraints. 
 "If you look at the terrestrial solutions, the curve is going the other direction. Everything's getting more expensive." 
 Johnsen made that argument in an earlier SEC-filed interview. 
 SpaceX's $74 Billion AI Gamble Has a Major Risk 
 SpaceX currently earns AI infrastructure revenue by renting computing power from ground-based facilities. Its latest financial filing reveals a significant vulnerability. 
 One customer, identified as "Customer B," generated 34.5% of third-quarter revenue, approximately $5 billion. 
 Bloomberg identified the customer as Anthropic, which is preparing for its Nasdaq debut. SpaceX has discussed its Anthropic relationship publicly but has not formally identified it as Customer B. 
 Johnsen has also said typical computing contracts can be terminated with 90 days' notice. 
 Meanwhile, spending is accelerating. SpaceX expects $35 billion to $40 billion in fourth-quarter capital expenditure and has separately announced two AI campuses costing more than $74 billion. 
 Its exclusive dependence on Nvidia chips adds another supply risk. 
 Options markets reflect considerable uncertainty. OptionCharts data indicates an implied range of roughly $61 to $221 by January 2029, rather than a firm price forecast. 
 SpaceX stock options expected move to January 19, 2029, range $61.08 to $220.90, Source: OptionCharts With SpaceX shares still around 37% below their $225.64 peak, investors face a critical question: can its current AI business generate enough sustainable revenue to support an expansion of this scale?
